# QC test for protein analysis

This Quarto document loads protein data from Luminex and Simoa measurements, checks for detectability (Figure S2), processes the data for subsequent analysis, and tests normality (Shapiro-Wilk)

# Load packages

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DataExplorer)
library(writexl)
```

# Define paths

```{r paths}
input_file    <- "Input/Cytokines_Predict-TB.xlsx"
output_fig_s2 <- "Output/Figure_S2"
output_tables <- "Output/Figure_S2/Tables"

dir.create(output_fig_s2, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(output_tables, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Load Data

```{r}
all_data <- read_excel(input_file, sheet = 1)

head(all_data)
dim(all_data)
```

```{r}
# Column names are updated to use standard cytokine nomenclature
names(all_data)

    IL_8       = L_IL_8,
    CCL2       = L_MCP_1,
    CCL3       = L_MIP_1_alpha,

names(protein_data)
```

# -- Detectability Analysis --

```{r}
# Extract LOD

lod_values <- protein_data %>%
  filter(Condition == "LOD") %>%
  select(BDNF:IFNB)

data_clean <- protein_data %>%
  filter(Condition != "LOD")
```

# Reshape to Long Format
```{r}
# Reshape-long

data_long <- data_clean %>%
  select(ID1, Condition, Visit, BDNF:IFNB) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = BDNF:IFNB,
    names_to  = "Cytokine",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

lod_long <- lod_values %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = everything(),
    names_to  = "Cytokine",
    values_to = "LOD"
  )
```

# Calculate Detectability

```{r}
detectability <- data_long %>%
  left_join(lod_long, by = "Cytokine") %>%
  group_by(Condition, Cytokine) %>%
  summarise(
    N_total       = sum(!is.na(Value)),
    N_detected    = sum(Value > LOD, na.rm = TRUE),
    Detectability = round(N_detected / N_total * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

detectability
```

# Save Detectability Results

The detectability table is saved as an Excel file for downstream use.

```{r}
# Save detectability

write_xlsx(
  detectability,
  path = file.path(output_tables, "Detectability_all_cytokines.xlsx")
)
```

# -- Figure S2: Detectability Heatmap --

```{r}
# Order conditions

detectability <- detectability %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = factor(
      Condition,
      levels = c("Null", "Mtb_Ag", "LPS", "IL1B")
    )
  )
```

# Build the Heatmap

```{r}
# Heatmap-detectability
heatmap_detect <- ggplot(
    detectability,
    aes(x = Condition, y = Cytokine, fill = Detectability)
  ) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(Detectability, "%")),
    color = "black",
    size  = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "#2166ac",
    mid      = "white",
    high     = "#b2182b",
    midpoint = 50,
    limits   = c(0, 100),
    name     = "Detectability (%)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Cytokine detectability by stimulation condition",
    subtitle = "Percentage of samples with values above the limit of detection",
    x        = "Stimulation condition",
    y        = "Cytokine"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "black"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "black"),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid      = element_blank()
  )

heatmap_detect
```

# Save the Heatmap

```{r}
# Save heatmap

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(output_fig_s2, "S2_Heatmap_detectability_all_cytokines.pdf"),
  plot     = heatmap_detect,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 8,
  units    = "in"
)
```

# -- Data cleaning and transformation --

```{r remove-low-detectability}
# Remove cytokines with low detectability. 
# Proteins with less than 50% detectability in all stimulation conditions were considered not consistently detectable and will be excluded from subsequent analyses. For IFNG and IL-2, Simoa measurements replaced Luminex in subsequent analyses due to superior detectability.

columns_to_remove <- c(
  "GM_CSF",
  "IL_17",
  "IL_5",
  "MMP_9",
  "SCF",
  "TNF_beta",
  "IL_2_L",
  "IFNG_L"
)

protein_data_filtered <- data_clean %>%
  select(-any_of(columns_to_remove))

names(protein_data_filtered)
```

# Rename cytokines with correct nomenclature

```{r rename-cytokines}
protein_data_new <- protein_data_filtered %>%
  rename(
    IFNG       = IFNG_S,
    IL_2       = IL_2_S
  )

names(protein_data_new)
```

# Define cytokine column names

```{r cytokine-cols}
# Defined cytokine columns
cytokine_cols <- c(
  "BDNF", "CCL11", "Factor_VII", "ICAM_1",
  "IL_1_alpha", "IL_1_beta", "IL_10", "IL_12p40",
  "IL_12p70", "IL_18", "IL_1RA", "IL_3", "IL_4",
  "IL_6", "IL_7", "IL_8", "CCL2", "CCL3",
  "MMP_3", "TNF", "VEGF", "IFNG", "IL_2",
  "pan_IFNA", "IFNB"
)

```

# Initial data overview

```{r intro-before-imputation}
plot_intro(protein_data_new[, cytokine_cols])
```

# Impute missing values for Simoa assay, by median values from the same Condition-Visit combination

```{r impute-function}
# cytokine_cols passed as argument to avoids a hardcoded list inside function
impute_by_groups <- function(data, cols) {
  data %>%
    group_by(Condition, Visit) %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(cols),
        ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .x)
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```

```{r apply-imputation}
protein_data_new <- impute_by_groups(protein_data_new, cytokine_cols)

cat("Total NAs remaining:", sum(is.na(protein_data_new[, cytokine_cols])), "\n")
```

# Data overview after imputation

```{r intro-after-imputation}
plot_intro(protein_data_new[, cytokine_cols])
```
# Check for zeros or negative values

```{r check-values}
n_zeros     <- sum(protein_data_new[, cytokine_cols] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_negatives <- sum(protein_data_new[, cytokine_cols] <  0, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("Zeros: %d | Negatives: %d\n", n_zeros, n_negatives))
```
# Log10 transform cytokine values

```{r log-transform}
# Due to very small and positive Simoa values, use log10 transformation, instead of log10(1+a)

protein_data_log <- protein_data_new %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(cytokine_cols), ~ log10(.x)))

head(protein_data_log)
```

# Save curated data frame for subsequent analysis
```{r}
write_xlsx(
  protein_data_log,
  path = file.path(output_tables, "Cytokines_cleaned_log10_Predict-TB.xlsx")
)
```

# -- Normality Test (Shapiro-Wilk) --

The Shapiro-Wilk test is applied to baseline samples (W0). The test is run
separately for each condition and cytokine combination.

# Filter to W0

```{r}
# Filter W0

data_visit0 <- data_long %>%
  filter(Visit == 0)

cat("Number of rows after filtering to W0:", nrow(data_visit0), "\n")
cat("Conditions present:", paste(unique(data_visit0$Condition), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# Remove Low-Variance Cytokines

```{r}

variance_per_cytokine <- data_visit0 %>%
  group_by(Cytokine) %>%
  summarise(
    Variance = var(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

low_variance_cytokines <- variance_per_cytokine %>%
  filter(Variance < 0.01) %>%
  pull(Cytokine)

cat(
  "Cytokines removed due to low variance (< 0.01):\n",
  paste(low_variance_cytokines, collapse = ", "), "\n"
)

data_visit0_filtered <- data_visit0 %>%
  filter(!Cytokine %in% low_variance_cytokines)

cat(
  "\nCytokines retained for normality testing:",
  n_distinct(data_visit0_filtered$Cytokine), "\n"
)
```

# Shapiro-Wilk Helper Function

```{r}
# Shapiro-function

run_shapiro <- function(x) {
  vals <- na.omit(x)
  n    <- length(vals)

  if (n < 3 || n > 5000) {
    reason <- ifelse(n < 3, "fewer than 3 observations", "more than 5000 observations")
    return(data.frame(
      SW_statistic = NA_real_,
      SW_p_value   = NA_real_,
      Note         = reason
    ))
  }

  if (length(unique(vals)) == 1) {
    return(data.frame(
      SW_statistic = NA_real_,
      SW_p_value   = NA_real_,
      Note         = "all values are identical"
    ))
  }

  result <- shapiro.test(vals)
  return(data.frame(
    SW_statistic = as.numeric(result$statistic),
    SW_p_value   = result$p.value,
    Note         = NA_character_
  ))
}
```

# Run the Normality Test
A p-value greater than 0.05 indicates that the data are consistent with a normal distribution.

```{r}
# Normality-test

normality_results <- data_visit0_filtered %>%
  group_by(Condition, Cytokine) %>%
  summarise(
    N         = sum(!is.na(Value)),
    sw_result = list(run_shapiro(Value)),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  unnest(sw_result) %>%
  mutate(
    Normal = case_when(
      is.na(SW_p_value) ~ "Not tested",
      SW_p_value > 0.05 ~ "Yes",
      TRUE              ~ "No"
    )
  )

normality_results
```

# Summarise Normality Results

A quick summary of how many cytokines pass or fail the normality test within
each condition.

```{r}
# Normality-summary

normality_results %>%
  filter(Normal != "Not tested") %>%
  count(Condition, Normal) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Normal,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

# Save Normality Results

```{r}
# Save normality

write_xlsx(
  normality_results,
  path = file.path(output_tables, "Normality_Shapiro_Wilk_Visit0.xlsx")
)
```
